headline: Decision models are duking it out, and they're practically giving them away
summary: Google jumps into decision models with a multimodal focus; an open-source Granola has arrived too.

items.title: Gemini launches a decision model API
items.pitch: Google just dropped a "decision model" (an AI built for yes/no calls and scoring), and it can look at videos and PDFs directly. It's so cheap it's basically free, perfect for dropping into your little tools.
why: Lets AI give docs/videos a yes/no or a score, and it's more reliable than chat models
It can judge text, images, audio, video, and PDFs
It joins similar models from Jev and OpenAI to make "decision models" a new category
actions: Read Simon Willison's hands-on test to see how it judges video content (simonwillison.net/tags/ai)
Grab one of your files and try a yes/no question on a small sample first to check accuracy
deep_dive: Unlike the Claude/codex you use: it doesn't chat, it quickly scores and sorts fixed questions.
Text and images put it in the same league as OpenAI's; multimodal (video/audio/PDF) is Gemini's unique trick.
Low barrier to entry, but you have to go through the API, so you'll need an agent to write a few lines of code to call it. Cheap doesn't mean accurate, so validate on a small sample first.
items.signals: HN 454 points · 142 comments · Simon Willison tested video judgment · smol.ai calls it "decision model day"

items.title: Yogurt: open-source meeting notes
items.pitch: An open-source alternative to Granola (the AI meeting notes app), free and focused on privacy. If you want to take meeting notes without uploading recordings to the cloud, take a look.
why: A free, open-source meeting notes AI, one more option to have
Privacy-first, good for sensitive stuff like salary talks
Self-hostable, so your data doesn't have to go to the cloud
actions: Check the install steps on GitHub (github.com/frigadehq)
Try it on one internal meeting first, don't jump straight to sensitive stuff
deep_dive: Unlike the cloud notes you use now: open source, self-hostable, and you get more control over privacy.
It's just an alternative to Granola, and it's an early project, so you'll have to test the transcription quality yourself.
Setup is medium-effort, you might need Docker or local config, and it's not click-and-go.
items.signals: Show HN 252 points · 96 comments · 19 hours ago

items.title: Google experiment: AI builds a shared space live
items.pitch: Google Labs' new experiment Tabletop: toss in links and files and the AI whips up an itinerary map, a poll board, or a chore chart on the spot. There's a waitlist for now.
why: Turns "let's do it someday" into a shared page you can actually use
Shows where AI-generated little tools are heading
items.signals: Announced by Google Labs · 1113 likes · 93 reposts · waitlist open
